stories.headline: 49ers owner Jed York suspended six games, fined $500K by NFL
stories.summary: 49ers owner Jed York has been suspended for six games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy stemming from his August arrest after he tried to engage in prostitution in Ohio.
stories.body:
San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York has been suspended for six games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy, the league announced Friday.

York was arrested in Ohio in August on suspicion of engaging in prostitution and pleaded no contest to a pair of misdemeanor charges.

He did not attend the 49ers' first three games of the season amid the NFL's investigation. Those games are credited toward his suspension, and he will be allowed to rejoin the team Oct. 20, the day after the 49ers face the Washington Commanders on "Monday Night Football."

York said in a statement that he accepted the NFL's decision and apologized to his family and the 49ers.

"This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility," York said. "What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family."

According to Columbiana County (Ohio) court records obtained by ESPN, York allegedly responded to an undercover ad on a known prostitution website and "arranged to have sexual activity with the female in exchange for $140" while using a pseudonym.

As part of his no-contest plea, York paid $1,150 in fines and was sentenced to one day in jail for each charge to be served concurrently, with one day already considered to be served.

York has been the majority owner of the Niners since 2024 but has been the team's CEO since 2008.

stories.headline: Erik ten Hag 'was a piece of crap' with Man United squad - Fred
stories.summary: Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a 'piece of crap' when it came to squad management.
stories.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a "piece of crap" when it came to squad management.

The Brazilian spent five years at United, winning the League Cup and reaching the FA Cup final in the 2022-23 season.

Ten Hag came to United with a big reputation, having managed Ajax for four seasons and taking them to the Champions League semifinals but, while he did win the FA Cup and League Cup in his two-and-a-half years in Manchester, things did not quite go as planned with regards to success in the Premier League.

And Fred, who left the club to join Turkish side Fenerbahce during Ten Hag's tenure ahead of the 2023-24 season, gave a damning review of his time under the Dutchman.

"Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of crap," he said on the "Charla Podcast."

"He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with Rashford ... He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.

"[With Ten Hag] Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.

- Sir Alex Ferguson on David Beckham's Preston loan: 'He thought I wanted him gone but that's not true'

- Sir Alex Ferguson was 'terrified' about Old Trafford return after brain surgery

- Rasmus Højlund hits 'Siuuu' against Portugal: 'Cristiano Ronaldo will never be forgotten'

"He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was already] older. He took Cristiano out [of the starting lineup], and then there was a falling out."

Ronaldo left the club at the end of the 2022 season after he found himself no longer in the starting lineup.

Ten Hag was sacked in October 2024, with United 14th after seven matches -- their worst start since the 1989-90 season.

Fred also lifted the lid on other United managers he experienced, including Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the 1999 treble winner who took the helm at the club in December 2018 after Jose Mourinho was sacked.

The 33-year-old, who has 32 Brazil caps, gave his assessment of both of those managers, who he had much more positive things to say about.

"Solskjaer was good with the group, but he was helped [in training] by the assistants. He united the group," Fred added.

"Mourinho's a great bloke, he is funny. I've just been with him at Fenerbahçe; he brought me to United.

"Before [Carlo] Ancelotti came along, his name was being mentioned for the national team [Brazil].

"So I'd show him the rumours and he'd say: 'F--- off, mate. I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to manage my club here.' A really decent bloke."

stories.headline: Red Sox's Mickey Gasper has surgery to repair right biceps tendon
stories.summary: Red Sox first baseman/catcher Mickey Gasper has undergone a repair of his right biceps tendon after he left the team's regular-season finale and did not appear in the playoffs.
stories.body:
BOSTON -- Red Sox first baseman/catcher Mickey Gasper has undergone what the team said Friday was a successful repair of his right biceps tendon.

Gasper started Boston's final regular-season series against the Chicago Cubs on Sept. 25 at catcher but was replaced in the sixth inning after experiencing discomfort in his biceps.

He was placed on the injured list and was not on the Red Sox's roster for their American League Wild Card Series loss to the New York Yankees.

The procedure was performed by Dr. Matthew Leibman at MassGeneral Brigham in Boston.

Gasper, a 30-year-old New Hampshire native, played a career-high 67 games in his third major league season, batting .251 with 10 home runs and 24 RBIs.

stories.headline: WNBA championship and Finals MVP odds: Aces backs as favorites after ousting Fever
stories.summary: The Las Vegas Aces are back to being the favorites for the WNBA title after advancing past the Indiana Fever.
stories.body:
The Las Vegas Aces are back to being the favorites for the WNBA title after defeating the Indiana Fever in a hard-fought first-round series, showing +160 odds at DraftKings. Bookmakers across the sportsbook marketplace are likely breathing a sigh of relief with the Fever eliminated, as Caitlin Clark's crew were a popular futures play all season and, thus, a huge liability.

The Atlanta Dream are second on the championship odds board at +240, followed by the Golden State Valkyries at +390. The New York Liberty were briefly the title favorites after taking down the previously favored Minnesota Lynx in two games, but they have fallen to fourth on the odds board at +450 with other teams advancing. The Dallas Wings round out the board at a distant 70-1.

In line with the championship odds, A'ja Wilson is the big favorite to be Finals MVP, with +175 odds. There's a three-way tie for second at +800 between Allisha Gray, Breanna Stewart and Gabby Williams, with Angel Reese and Rhyne Howard rounding out the top six at 10-1.

Slater on the Warriors' options this season: "I think we mentioned it last time we talked about the Warriors, but think about what the Lakers did with LeBron. I know we just questioned some of the deals they signed, but the fact that they could sign all those deals was because LeBron James took all his money and walked away. So you could let Jimmy [Butler] somewhat walk away.

Obviously Jimmy's going to want every dollar he can get, but there's a chance Jimmy and Draymond could take pay cuts next season, right? The market might demand that they do.

"I've had these conversations with Steve [Kerr] and again I think you're going to hear it a lot publicly in their messaging, they're going to adapt the offense at times away from Draymond. Oct. 1

Duren, Pistons end standoff with long-term deal

All-NBA center Jalen Duren has agreed to a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Detroit Pistons, his agent told ESPN's Shams Charania. Duren had until 11:59 p.m. ET Thursday to decide on the Pistons' one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

Mitch Johnson excited about Billy Donovan's role with Spurs
San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan.

"I don't want to be naive enough to think I'm going to tell you what a 61-year old Hall of Fame coach like Billy Donovan and his resume can bring to the table," Johnson said. "I'm excited he's here. He's a tremendous person, great personality, fits in seamlessly. He's got worlds of experience and he's an extremely hard worker. He's not kicking up his feet and telling stories. He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year."

Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4).

Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games.

A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder, after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Wright

Shead agrees to three-year extension in Toronto

Guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million extension with the Toronto Raptors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Shead averaged 6.6 points and 5.6 assists per game last season.

Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal

Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived.

Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost.

The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN.

Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal?

On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks.

"Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30.

Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice
Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday.

"He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see."

After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries.

He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain.

The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona, who is dealing with a sprained left foot.

Anfernee Simons, who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp.

"Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that."

Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season.

Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise.

"With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right?

"But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

Sept. 28

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade

Jayson Tatum's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

"The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday. "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years."

Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team
It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch.

The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%.

Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience.

Williamson not where he wants to be
New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.
"I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab

Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery, Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp.

"I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly."

Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon.

It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process.

A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule.

"My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater

Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Sept. 26

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Charles Leclerc tops second practice, Mercedes off the pace
stories.summary: Charles Leclerc topped the timesheets in second practice at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, with the session staying dry despite the threat of rain.
stories.body:
Charles Leclerc topped the timesheets in second practice at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, with the session staying dry despite the threat of rain.

The Ferrari driver set the time halfway through the session on the soft compound tyre and crossed the line 0.099 seconds ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar.

McLaren's Lando Norris was third-fastest, with Max Verstappen behind. The Dutchamn, who was fastest in first practice, spent the session doing long runs on the medium tyre, while the majority of the grid were on the soft tyres.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton rounded out the top five and was three-tenths off his teammate Leclerc's pace.

McLaren made some adjustments to Norris' rear wing to get the 'Macarena' style rear wing that Oscar Piastri was using in first practice on Friday.

Piastri ended the second session in sixth, while Mercedes duo George Russell and title leader Kimi Antonelli were off the pace and finished down in seventh and eighth respectively. Both drivers were on soft tyres but had to abort their flying laps.

- Bahrain GP in Malaysia: Max Verstappen leads first practice from George Russell

- Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained

- Lewis Hamilton hits out at Ferrari hierarchy in Fred Vasseur defence: 'Point fingers somewhere else'

Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto complained on the team radio that Hamilton got in his way on track, while the seven-time champion reported that "he can't see through" his right mirror. Hamilton was sent to the stewards and has received a warning, while Ferrari were fined €10,000 (£8,503).

Bortoleto also brought out the Virtual Safety Car in the closing stages of the session.

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson was ninth and Alpine's Pierre Gasly rounded out the top 10.

stories.headline: MMA 30 under 30: Champions Joshua Van and Usman Nurmagomedov lead
stories.summary: The future is now! Joshua Van, Usman Nurmagomedov and more championship-caliber fighters top 30 under 30 list.
stories.body:
ESPN's yearly list of the top 30 fighters under age 30 can be characterized as a look into the future. These are the young fighters who presumably will take over once the sport's top veterans move on.

But this year's ranking is not merely forward thinking.

Consider that the top two fighters -- Joshua Van in the UFC and Usman Nurmagomedov in the PFL -- aren't rising prospects. They are defending champions. No. 3 Ilia Topuria is a former UFC champion. And Natalia Silva, who sits at No. 9, will go for the vacant women's flyweight title this weekend at UFC 332. In MMA, it seems, "the future is now" is not simply a catchy slogan.

There also are up-and-comers in these rankings, as there are every year, and many who have appeared before are now in different positions, as a year's worth of fight results dictates.

Our panel -- Brett Okamoto, Dre Waters, Jeff Wagenheim, Andrew Davis, James Regan, Sam Bruce, James Dielhenn, Marcus Vanderberg and Alecia Hamm -- selected fighters based on their achievements this year and their potential. Okamoto, Waters and Wagenheim provide breakdowns of the top 30 under 30.

1. Joshua Van

UFC men's flyweight champion

Age: 24

2025 rank: 3

It takes a remarkable athlete to lead this type of list -- but to lead it at 24 years old is just absurd. Van is arguably the purest talent the sport has seen in years. No one could have predicted at the start of 2025, when his ascension truly took off, that he would end the year as ESPN's best breakout fighter. He is undeniably the best active flyweight on the planet and has the personality and charisma to match. Sean O'Malley recently proclaimed on his YouTube channel that Van will go down as the "greatest flyweight of all time." After Van's second win over former longtime champion Alexandre Pantoja at UFC 331, who wants to disagree? -- Okamoto

2. Usman Nurmagomedov

PFL lightweight champion

Age: 28

2025 rank: 7

It's unusual for a fighter outside the UFC to establish himself as the best in his weight class, but that's exactly what Nurmagomedov has done with his perfect 21-0 record. It's not unreasonable to suggest Nurmagomedov would be favored against any other 155-pound fighter in the world, including top-ranked UFC lightweights Justin Gaethje, Arman Tsarukyan and Ilia Topuria. Nurmagomedov is currently a free agent, and his next move is one of the biggest questions in MMA this year. -- Okamoto

3. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 1

Topuria entered the year as the UFC lightweight champion, ESPN's top-ranked fighter under 30 and on the short list of the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world. He got his first chance to defend the belt in a main event at the White House on June 14, but the challenger, Gaethje, handed him the first loss of his professional career, retiring him on the stool after four rounds. Despite the loss, Topuria remains one of MMA's best young fighters. -- Waters

4. Michael Morales

UFC welterweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: 5

Fans love a good knockout, and Morales has handed out KOs regularly on his way to the welterweight title picture. Three consecutive first-round finishes have all the momentum on Morales's side, but he hasn't fought yet this year. He's on champion Islam Makhachev's radar as a future welterweight challenger, but he'll likely need one more win against a top contender to get his first title shot. -- Okamoto

5. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL women's flyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 2

One of the most destructive figures in women's MMA, Ditcheva is uniquely violent, boasting a 73% knockout rate in the PFL. The question isn't whether she can be a star, it's how big her star can become. With Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions acquiring the PFL going into 2027, we will find out what the ceiling is for Ditcheva's exposure. She is exactly the kind of marketable athlete MVP will get behind. -- Okamoto

6. Song Yadong

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 28

Song put two years of little activity behind him by fighting three times in the first eight months of 2026. He lost a tight decision to Sean O'Malley in January, but he bounced back in May against another champion, choking out Deiveson Figueiredo. But what elevated Song most on this list -- he was way down at No. 28 last year -- was his knockout of Umar Nurmagomedov in August. That stunning result boosted Song's stock as a men's bantamweight contender. Next up should be another ranked opponent, giving him an opportunity to build off of his recent success. -- Wagenheim

7. Josh Hokit

UFC heavyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Hokit's antics on the microphone may not have endeared him to UFC CEO Dana White, who said at UFC 331 that he doesn't like anything Hokit says. But the heavyweight's performance in his second year in the Octagon has skyrocketed him to the top of the division. "I say it all the time: I don't have to like you for you to thrive here and you to do well and be successful," White said of Hokit's ascension. With just four UFC fights under his belt -- three this year -- Hokit is set to challenge Ciryl Gane for the heavyweight championship in the main event at UFC 334 in November. Hokit, who earned a contract on Season 9 of "Dana White's Contender Series" just 13 months ago, already has beaten heavyweight stalwarts Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis in two of the more entertaining fights of the year. Ending 2026 with a UFC championship would be an impressive cap to his year. -- Waters

8. Ian Machado Garry

UFC welterweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 6

Love him or hate him, Machado Garry might be the best UFC welterweight not named Islam Makhachev. He took the pound-for-pound king five competitive rounds in August and is still in great position to accept some of the biggest fights available as he works his way back toward a second title shot. Machado Garry has said he believes that a loss to Makhachev will only make him better, and there are plenty of reasons to believe the 28-year-old's best is still in front of him. -- Okamoto

9. Natalia Silva

UFC women's flyweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 9

Silva might be a UFC champion by the end of the weekend. By winning 14 fights in a row, the past eight in the Octagon, she has been looking more and more like championship material. Her three most recent wins came against former titleholders Jessica Andrade, Alexa Grasso and Rose Namajunas. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva is poised to take over if she handles Wang Cong at UFC 332. Women's flyweight is a highly competitive division, with several pound-for-pound elites. It could be Silva's domain until someone figures out how to contend with her slick movement. -- Wagenheim

10. Quillan Salkilld

UFC lightweight

Age: 26

2025 rank: 23

Somehow, even in a division full of potential superstars, Australia's Salkilld has managed to stand out -- and not just because he has a great mustache. Salkilld's got a look and presence on social media that plays well with the UFC's fanbase, and he has substance to back up the flash. He is on a streak of five consecutive first-round finishes, including in his most recent win, in which he beat submission artist Mateusz Gamrot at his own game with a first-round rear-naked choke. Salkilld has that "it" factor, and if he keeps winning, he will collide with some of the sport's biggest names. -- Okamoto

11. Jean Silva

UFC featherweight

Age: 29

Last year's rank: 15

Silva was denied a higher-profile opportunity when his Noche UFC opponent, popular and flashy Yair Rodriguez, withdrew from last month's fight because of injury. Silva did not suffer a letdown against late replacement Jose Miguel Delgado, taking care of business by doing what he usually does: making the fight his showcase. The win was Silva's second in a row after a September 2025 knockout loss ended a 13-fight winning streak. Silva is building himself toward featherweight contention with an aggressive fighting style that is a dream for fans and a nightmare for opponents. -- Wagenheim

12. Tatsuro Taira

UFC men's flyweight

Age: 26

Last year's rank: 22

Taira won eight of his first nine UFC fights, a run of success capped by a knockout of former two-time men's flyweight champion Brandon Moreno in December. But it was a loss that drew more attention to him -- positive attention. Taira ended up being knocked out by current champion Joshua Van in a title fight in May, but it was a back-and-forth fight that lasted into the fifth round. Taira put the champ in trouble with eight takedowns and over 10 minutes of control time. It was fight of the night, keeping the Japanese fighter in the contender conversation. -- Wagenheim

13. Navajo Stirling

UFC light heavyweight

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

Entering 2026, all three of Stirling's UFC wins had come by unanimous decision, but that stretch seems like an anomaly now. Stirling earned a UFC contract via a second-round knockout on "Dana White's Contender Series" in 2024 and had knocked out three of his four professional opponents before that. He officially refound his finishing ways this year, winning each of his three fights by knockout, including a first-round TKO over former light heavyweight champion Jan Blachowicz in August. Stirling may not have opened the year nearing his first title shot, but if he can take down another former champion in JiYí Procházka on Nov. 21, he'll end the year near the top of the light heavyweight contenders short list. -- Waters

14. Thad Jean

PFL welterweight champion

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

The PFL has asked several figures to be the "face of the company" over the years with mixed results. Recently much of that promotional expectation has been heaped on Jean, the 28-year-old who won the 2025 welterweight tournament. Jean has legitimate skills and highlight-reel potential. He's styled on the opponents he should have, and has proven his world-class merit with hard-fought wins over tougher opponents such as Logan Storley and Jason Jackson. -- Okamoto

15. Gabriel Bonfim

UFC welterweight

Age: 29

Last year's rank: 21

Bonfim is another fighter on this list who could be nearing a title shot. He only has competed once this year, but was dominant in a five-round unanimous decision win over former welterweight champion Belal Muhammad. All three judges scored the fight 50-45 for Bonfirm, who claimed the No. 7 spot in ESPN's divisional rankings as a result. Bonfim's biggest hurdle going forward will be the rise in competition in a stacked 170-pound division. His next test will come against No. 6-ranked Sean Brady on Nov. 7. -- Waters

16. Salahdine Parnasse

UFC lightweight

Age: 28

Last year's rank: NR

It's been an interesting year for Parnasse. In January, he defended his lightweight championship in the Polish fight promotion KSW, winning by knockout. He vacated that title to fight on the first MMA card for Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions brand. Parnasse scored a first-round knockout over Kenneth Cross on the undercard of the most-watched MMA event ever. Last month he made his UFC debut, scoring another knockout -- his sixth in a row. The first-round finish of Dan Hooker doesn't make Parnasse a contender, but he's someone to keep watching. -- Wagenheim

17. Ateba Gautier

UFC middleweight

Age: 24

Last year's rank: NR

Gautier is an absolute wrecking ball of a human. Nine of his 11 career wins have come by knockout, including seven in the first round. Potential? Off the charts. Momentum? Undeniable. The only question around Gautier isn't about him, but his opposition. His five UFC opponents have a 4-14 combined record inside the Octagon. That will change when he meets Roman Kopylov (15-5) this weekend at UFC 332. If Gautier knocks out Kopylov, his hype will be validated. -- Okamoto

18. Erin Blanchfield

UFC women's flyweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: 11

Blanchfield has been included on ESPN's list of top young prospects nearly every year since she signed with the UFC in 2021. She was ESPN's No. 1 prospect under 25 in 2023, but missed the cut the following year after suffering a one-sided drubbing to Manon Fiorot. She bounced back from that loss with back-to-back wins over Rose Namajunas and Tracy Cortez and is scheduled to take on Jasmine Jasudavicius on Oct. 17 in a battle of top-10 flyweights. -- Waters

19. Payton Talbott

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: 20

You know a young fighter is someone the UFC considers a rising prospect when you start to see him booked against championship-decorated opponents. Talbott is coming off a December win that was convincing enough to send former two-division titlist Henry Cejudo into retirement. This weekend at UFC 332, Talbott will take on another former belt-holder, Deiveson Figueiredo. These kinds of fights draw attention, even when they're against faded stars. If Talbott is successful again, he could be on his way toward ranked opposition and a slow, steady build. -- Wagenheim

20. Lone'er Kavanagh

UFC men's flyweight

Age: 27

2025 rank: NR

He can't live on one performance forever, but Kavanagh's five-round victory over former champion Brandon Moreno in February -- in Mexico, on short notice -- said a lot about this 27-year-old's capabilities. He's 1-2 in his past three appearances, but Kavanagh has a tantalizing amount of potential. How big would a Joshua Van vs. Lone'er Kavanagh title fight be, if Kavanagh were to get on a roll and give England a shot at its next UFC champion? -- Okamoto

21. Paul Hughes

PFL lightweight

Age: 29

2025 rank: 16

Hughes came up short in two attempts to take the PFL lightweight championship from Nurmagomedov last year. Despite losing both fights by decision, Hughes proved himself to be one of the best lightweights in the world. He has been out of action this year due to a knee injury, but now that Nurmagomedov is a free agent, there's a chance for Hughes to challenge for the PFL title again immediately upon returning to active status. -- Waters

22. Gable Steveson

UFC heavyweight

Age: 26

2025 rank: NR

Steveson was about 12 seconds from being a whole lot higher on this list. As an Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was as highly anticipated a prospect as the sport has seen when he transitioned to MMA last year. After winning his first four pro fights by first-round knockout, including his UFC debut in July, Steveson looked like a heavyweight with which to be reckoned. He still might turn into that guy, but getting KO'd by the second punch heavy underdog Sean Sharaf threw at him at UFC 331 two weeks ago put the brakes on the Steveson hype train. The big dude has work to do. -- Wagenheim

23. Muhammad Mokaev

Brave CF men's flyweight champion

Age: 26

2025 rank: 27

One of the most unique -- and frustrating -- careers in MMA continues to play out outside the UFC. It's now been 26 months since Mokaev parted ways with the promotion. It's worth noting that Mokaev's last fight in the UFC was a victory over Manel Kape, who is widely expected to be the next title challenger for Van. Will we ever see a day when Mokaev can return? At the moment, there doesn't seem to be much of a thaw from the UFC side. But Mokaev is still 26 years old and still unbeaten. He's so young and freakishly good that it's impossible to count out any opportunity forever. -- Okamoto

24. Valter Walker

UFC heavyweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Walker has been the epitome of a one-trick fighter so far in his UFC career. But if his one trick isn't broken, why fix it? Since losing by unanimous decision in his UFC debut in 2024, Walker has been on an absolute tear, beating each of his past five opponents by first-round submission. Four of those finishes have come via heel hook. It wasn't until his most recent victory over Thomas Petersen that the submission ace had to show more of his ability, transitioning from his signature heel hook attempt into a calf slicer submission for the finish. -- Waters

25. David Martinez

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Look no further than the UFC's matchmaking to decipher how promising Martinez is. The UFC tried to pair him with Umar Nurmagomedov in July, but Martinez was forced to withdraw because of injury. He has quietly taken out some of the most respected veterans in the bantamweight division -- Dan Ige, Marlon Vera and Rob Font -- over the past 12 months and is on the cusp of a top-five ranking. Martinez lacks some of the star power of other names on this list, but he's likely to draw big-name opponents in the near future. Consistent results would inevitably skyrocket every aspect of his career. -- Okamoto

26. Tommy McMillen

UFC featherweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

McMillen, who trains with former UFC men's bantamweight champion Sean O'Malley, has had a breakout performance this year. He earned a UFC contract on "Dana White's Contender Series" a year ago and has strung together three straight wins since. He was tested in his most recent bout, a unanimous decision win over Marwan Rahiki, but he outpointed Rahiki on all three of the judges' scorecards. He's earned the right to take a step up in competition in his next Octagon appearance. -- Waters

27. Jose Miguel Delgado
UFC featherweight

Age: 28

2025 rank: NR

Delgado was victorious in four of his first five trips to the Octagon before running into Jean Silva in the main event of Noche UFC last month. Fighting on short notice, Delgado lost by third-round submission, but he won the first round and held his own until running low on energy, whereupon Silva took over. His success in the early rounds gives Delgado building blocks for the future. -- Wagenheim

28. Raul Rosas Jr.

UFC men's bantamweight

Age: 21

2025 rank: 30

Still just 21 years old, Rosas is 7-1 in the UFC -- and the context around some of those wins is starting to grow. No longer is Rosas a phenom teenager operating on UFC prelims. Coming off his first UFC main event on Sept. 26, Rosas now holds two significant wins over proven veterans in Rob Font and Raoni Barcelos and is a ranked UFC bantamweight ... all before his 22nd birthday next week. There is no comparison to Rosas when it comes to experience gained at such a young age. There are plenty of steps between where he is now and a UFC championship, but he's certainly on the right path. -- Okamoto

29. Baisangur Susurkaev

UFC middleweight

Age: 25

2025 rank: 25

Susurkaev, a longtime training partner of former champion Khamzat Chimaev, made a name for himself last summer when he earned a UFC contract on "Dana White's Contender Series" then made his official debut four days later at UFC 319. He finished both of his opponents in those contests. In his lone appearance this year, Susurkaev picked up another finish, beating Djorden Santos by third-round submission in May. Next, he'll take on a fellow unbeaten prospect Donte Johnson at UFC 334 in November. A win over Johnson could establish Susurkaev as a future problem for top middleweight fighters. -- Waters

30. Iasmin Lucindo

UFC strawweight

Age: 24

2025 rank: 29

Lucindo had won five of six fights and was on the rise before an injury and a failed drug test in September 2025 derailed her. She withdrew from a fight with strawweight contender Gillian Robertson and ended up being suspended for a year, while Robertson went on to a title challenge. Lucindo is eligible to compete again, and at 24 years old she has time to build herself back up to contendership in the 115-pound division. -- Wagenheim

stories.headline: AFL player movement tracker: trade requests, free agency latest, who's on the move?
stories.summary: The offseason is upon us which means AFL trades, free agency, and player movement is about to take off. Here's the latest news, whispers, and confirmed deals.
stories.body:
It's AFL player movement season, with trades and free agency set to dominate the month of October. So who is going where? Keep track with our player movement guide here.

When is the AFL trade and free agency window?
The 2026 AFL trade period commences on Monday, October 5 and closes in the evening of Wednesday, October 14.

The free agency window opens and closes a little earlier; it runs from Friday, October 2 until Friday, October 9.

Friday, Oct. 2
FREE AGENCY OPEN
Greene on his way to the Cats

Toby Greene will join Geelong as an unrestricted free agent on a three-year deal, re-partnering with former Giants teammate Jeremey Cameron.

The paperwork was lodged to the AFL on Friday morning.

The Giants receive band three compensation for Greene, which is currently pick No. 26 in the upcoming draft.

Greene departs the Giants with his name etched in the club's record books, sitting first in games played for the club with a tally of 282 games, as well as leading the club's all-time goalkicking tally with 450 majors.

Briggs now a Tiger

Richmond has landed GWS ruck Kieren Briggs as an unrestricted free agent.

Briggs' move to the Tigers was confirmed just hours after the free agency window opened on Friday.

Briggs played 88 games for GWS after joining the club as the No.34 pick in the 2018 draft.

Amartey officially joins the Blues

Free agency has opened with a bang, with out-of-favour key forward Joel Amartey committing to Carlton.

Details are still to come on the length of contract, and Sydney's compensation.

Hawthorn father-son recommits despite interest

Calsher Dear has made a shock decision to re-sign with the Hawks for two years, despite being out of favour thorughout 2026.

The 20-year-old has kicked 39 goals from 31 games, but found himself behind Jack Gunston, Mitch Lewis and Mabior Chol. With Gunston signed on and Suns forward Ben King expected to sign with the Hawks as well, there were questions about whether Dear would get enough opportunity at his childhood club.

Hawks list boss Mark McKenzie said the club was "really pleased" that Dear had recommitted.

"He remains an important part of what we are trying to achieve as a club," he said.

"Following his debut season, Calsher showed us all the special talent that he is, but as a key tall at 21 years of age, we've needed to be patient with his progression.

"Having battled several injuries over his first three seasons in the system, we are very excited about what the future holds for Calsher with a strong pre-season under his belt and greater continuity into 2027 and beyond."

Thursday, Oct. 1
Goater set to make cross-city switch

North Melbourne defender Josh Goater is set to join the Hawks after requesting a trade on Thursday.

Having played just 18 games, the 23-year-old had fallen out of favour after an injury-hit run in his time at North.

Premiership Lion requests trade

The Brisbane Lions have confirmed Sam Marshall has requested a trade to St Kilda.

"The Brisbane Lions confirm premiership midfielder Sam Marshall has requested to be traded to St Kilda," the Lions said in a statement.

"Marshall has played 13 games, including the 2025 Premiership, across two seasons since being selected in the first round of the 2024 draft as a graduate of the Youi Brisbane Lions Academy.

"The club respects Marshall's request to be traded, and will work towards facilitating an outcome that best reflects true value to the Brisbane Lions for the 20-year-old."

Tuesday, Sept. 29
Neale informs Lions he intends to join Collingwood

Two-time Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale has told Brisbane he will depart the club as an unrestricted free agent and sign a three-year deal with Collingwood.

Aware that Neale intended to leave at the end of the year, the Lions never offered him a new contract.

The paperwork for the deal is expected to be formalised as early as Friday when the free agency period opens.

Friday, Sept. 25
Jordon Butts to join the Bulldogs

Zak Butters isn't the only South Australian-based player keen to join the Western Bulldogs, with Crows' key defender Jordon Butts officially naming the Dogs as his preferred offseason destination.

The unrestricted free agent will sign a five-year deal at the Kennel, according to AFL.com.au.

Tuesday, Sept. 22
Amartey officially names Carlton

Wantaway Sydney forward Joel Amartey has confirmed his desire to join Carlton as an unrestricted free agent.

The 26-year-old was kept out of the Swans' side with an Achilles injury in the latter stages of the year.

With Charlie Curnow (75 goals in 2026) and Logan McDonald (51) cementing their spots in the Sydney forward line as the prime targets, Amartey is hoping for more opportunity at the Blues.

Thursday, Sept. 17
GWS captain finally makes big call on his future

Toby Greene has opted to leave GWS, telling the AFL club he wishes to play with Geelong next season. Greene, who has been at the Giants since their foundation season in 2012, wants to go back to Victoria for family reasons.

In an extraordinary way to announce the decision, outgoing GWS boss Dave Matthews confirmed Greene's intentions on radio, before the club released a statement.

The 32-year-old has been offered a lucrative three-year deal to join the Cats.

Saturday, Sept. 12
Zak Butters makes huge free agency call
The year's hottest restricted free agent Zak Butters has made a huge call on his future, nominating the Western Bulldogs as his preferred destination.

After a year of speculation, with Geelong thought to be the front-runner for the Power star's signature, Butters made the call on Saturday, first reported by AFL.com.au's Callum Twomey.

The deal is reportedly for nine years.

Thursday, Sept. 10
Hogan set to join Pies
GWS and Collingwood have both confirmed that 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan has chosen the Magpies at his next home.

Set to be a four-club player, Hogan is 31 and coming off a 12-goal season from just nine appearances.

It's a big boost for the Magpies if Hogan can recapture his form; key forward has been an area of concern for a number of years.

Tuesday, Sept. 8
Bailey set to be Lion for life
Brisbane's Zac Bailey has ended months of 'will he, won't he' speculation to sign with the Lions for eight years, taking him through the 2034 season, the the club confirmed on Tuesday.

Bailey, a free agent, had been a big target for the Crows, who had reportedly tabled a more lucrative offer.

"I'm absolutely rapt to be staying at the Brisbane Lions," Bailey said in a statement.

"I love the environment here, the players, coaches and staff who all make it a great place to be and I feel like this Club continues to bring the best out of me.

"This Club means so much to me - I came here as a young player and have grown up here and to know I will be here long-term is something I'm really proud of.

"I would like to thank the club, my partner Em, my family and my management for being so supportive throughout this process.

"I love what we as a club have achieved during my time here and I am super excited about what we can continue to achieve together."

Rowan Marshall requests trade
St Kilda ruck Rowan Marshall looks set to be on the move, with the Saints confirming the big man had requested a trade for the second straight season.

While Marshall hasn't requested a specific club, it's likely to be Geelong after he failed to secure a trade to the Cats last year. He played 21 games for the Saints this seaosn, juggling ruck duties with Tom De Koning, who came in from Carlton last offseason.

"Rowan is a highly valued member of the St Kilda Football Club and remains contracted until the end of 2027," the Saints said in a statement.

"Marshall has not nominated a preferred destination at this stage, with the club making clear that any trade will need to be in the best interests of the St Kilda Football Club."

Zane Duursma wants to go to Melbourne
The No. 4 pick in the 2023 AFL draft Zane Duursma has requested a trade out of North Melbourne, with Melbourne in his sights.

The news comes a week after coach Alastair Clarkson was sacked by the club. North won nine games in 2026, their best return since 2019.

Ed Allan re-signs with the Pies
After speculation about his future at the Magpies, mdifielder Ed Allan has put pen to paper, signing a four year extension to remain at Collingwood.

2026 was a breakout season for Allan, who played 19 games and averaged a career-high 16.5 disposals per game.

Monday, Sept. 7
Pair of in-demand Dogs re-sign
According to afl.com.au, both Arty Jones and Buku Khamis will remain at the Kennel this offseason.

Jones will sign a three-year deal, while Khamis has a five-year contract in front of him.

Essendon and Brisbane had interest in livewire forward Jones, who had a standout performance against Collingwood in the wildcard final win, while the Blues were heavily linked to Khamis for a second straight offseason.

Cooper Hodge nomintes Hawthorn
A big boost for the Hawks, with club champion Luke Hodge's son Cooper choosing to join the Melbourne-based team as a father-son at this year's draft.

He had the option of going to Brisbane as a Lions academy member.

stories.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
stories.summary: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
stories.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

"The UEFA statement confirms receipt of documentation submitted by Real Madrid and indicates that the investigators will assess it within the framework of the existing investigation. The same text expressly refers, on two occasions, to an investigation and a review that are 'ongoing.' It therefore does not announce the opening, reopening, or reactivation of any proceedings, nor does it contain any assessment of the substance or value of the documentation provided.

"It is up to the investigators to determine what action, if any, they consider appropriate regarding this documentation. As of today, they have not made any new requests to FC Barcelona nor have they forwarded Real Madrid's complaint to the Club. Should they do so, the Club will respond accordingly, as it has done up to now.

"In accordance with the applicable legislation governing this matter, these proceedings are subject to the outcome of the criminal case currently being heard in Spain and will continue to be so."

stories.headline: Concussed Roosters star learns Grand Final fate
stories.summary: Sydney Roosters utility Connor Watson will miss the NRL grand final after failing to receive the green light to return to play inside the code's 11-day concussion stand-down period.
stories.body:
Sydney Roosters utility Connor Watson will miss the NRL Grand Final after failing to receive the green light to return to play inside the code's 11-day concussion stand-down period.

In a cruel blow, Watson will miss Sunday's decider against his former club Newcastle and become the first player to sit out a grand final as a result of a concussion.

Watson was dazed and was taken from the field moments after coming on in the Roosters' preliminary final win over the Dolphins.

Under the NRL's protocol, players diagnosed with a category-one concussion, as Watson was, face a mandatory stand-down period of 11 days.

The Roosters had indicated that Watson was testing well leading into Thursday when the 30-year-old met with an independent specialist.

But on Friday the club confirmed the utility had failed to receive clearance to line up in the grand final.

The outcome means Watson has played his last game for the Roosters with the popular utility heading to St George Illawarra next season before linking up with the PNG Chiefs in 2028.

Watson's absence likely forces Roosters coach Trent Robinson's hand when it comes to his bench, with hooker Benaiah Ioelu the most obvious man to come into Easts' 19-man squad.

Ioelu has played mostly off the bench through his 17-game NRL career and would act as cover for Reece Robson.

"I don't think it takes too much to work out what plan B is, but we have got some really good hookers," Robinson said on Thursday.

"Benaiah Ioelu played some great footy for us this year. He brings a lot of energy to us as well so he will come into consideration then."

Newcastle, meanwhile, are also expected to face a tough decision leading into Sunday's decider as they weigh up a replacement for suspended No. 9 Phoenix Crossland.

Harrison Graham has excelled as a bench option at hooker for the Knights, but coach Justin Holbrook, who doesn't have to name his final team until 90 minutes before kick-off on Sunday, has the option of also starting Thomas Cant or Diesel Hagan.

stories.headline: Shoulder injuries sideline Gonzalez, Barmore as Pats ready for Bills
stories.summary: The New England Patriots will be without starting cornerback Christian Gonzalez and defensive tackle Christian Barmore due to a shoulder injury when they visit the Bills on Sunday.
stories.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- The New England Patriots will be without starting cornerback Christian Gonzalez due to a shoulder injury when they visit the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, coach Mike Vrabel said.

Gonzalez did not practice all week. He made a physical tackle in the first quarter of last week's blowout loss to the Jaguars but stayed in the game after that play.

In addition, defensive tackle Christian Barmore won't play due to a shoulder injury, per Vrabel.

"That's what the situation is, there's nothing we can do about it," Vrabel said after Friday's practice. "We can make sure that the guys that are playing are ready. That happens every week in the National Football League. I'm looking forward to seeing the guys that are going to play in there."

Vrabel said slot corner Marcus Jones could be tapped to play more on the outside to help fill Gonzalez's void, while third-year player Charles Woods also is anticipated to play alongside starter Carlton Davis III.

"Gonzo is a playmaker, for sure, so we know we're going to miss him out there," Davis said. "But we preach all the time 'next guy up' and Charles Woods has been playing good every time he has to step in for one of us. We're going to trust him and go into this game trying to win it, for sure."

Vrabel also mentioned rookie Karon Prunty, a fifth-round pick from Wake Forest, as someone who could be called upon to step in as a depth option in addition to his special teams duties.

The Patriots, who won the AFC East last season, are 1-2 and would fall further behind the 3-0 Bills in the standings with a loss. Through three games, Buffalo is fourth in the league in total offense.

stories.headline: Former Man City boss Roberto Mancini: Unconcerned by guilty verdict
stories.summary: Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.
stories.body:
ROME -- Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.

In his latest comments on the issue, Mancini said: "It's not a problem that concerns me" -- despite appearing to acknowledge last weekend before a Nations League match in Turkey that he had "a double contract" as City coach from 2009-13.

Among the raft of charges that City has faced is an alleged failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

In 2018, German magazine Der Spiegel published evidence showing Mancini doubled his base salary of £1.45 million (now $1.9 million) for advising a club in Abu Dhabi.

City has been accused of potentially avoiding paying about £12 million ($16 million) in income tax and national insurance in relation to Mancini's salary, The Telegraph reported this week.

Mancini was asked if he was worried about the case ahead of Italy's match in France on Friday.

"No. I already spoke it about the other night. It's not something that concerns me. It's City's problem, unfortunately," Mancini said late Thursday at the Stade de France.

"It's not a problem that concerns me," Mancini added, repeating himself. "Look, really. I already said it the other day in Turkey."

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Man City appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

In Turkey, Mancini said that "Manchester City is not guilty and the fact of having a double contract isn't my problem but theirs, probably."

Mancini led City to its first titles after Abu Dhabi's ruling family had bought the club in 2008, winning the FA Cup in 2011 and in 2011-12 coaching the team to its first Premier League title in a half century.

He was fired days after a shocking loss to Wigan in the FA Cup final in 2013.

City has protested its innocence throughout the long-running case, which reached a milestone Tuesday when the Premier League published a verdict saying the club was "guilty of all charges related to serious breaches" of the competition's financial rules from 2009-18.

stories.headline: Every team's odds to win the World Series: Dodgers still favorites as ALDS and NLDS begin
stories.summary: Every MLB team's odds to win the 2026 World Series as the playoffs begin.
stories.body:
As they were before the season, the Los Angeles Dodgers begin their postseason run as the consensus favorite to win the 2026 World Series. The Dodgers enter the playoffs at +200 to win the title -- not much shorter than the +230 odds they had coming into the 2026 season. The New York Yankees, another preseason favorite, are next at +500, tied with the Milwaukee Brewers, owners of MLB's best regular-season record.

The American League-leading Tampa Bay Rays round out the top four at +800. While bookmakers expected Los Angeles and New York to make it this far, they were more bearish on Milwaukee and Tampa Bay in the preseason, assigning them 35-1 and 80-1 championship odds, respectively.

The Atlanta Braves come in next at +850, followed by the Cleveland Guardians at 11-1. While neither of those teams have attracted too much action, some books have taken wagers and have World Series liability on the San Diego Padres, checking in at 11-1.

With the exception of the Brewers and Yankees at some books, the favorites aren't generally causing liability. However, there's one team every single bookmaker will be rooting against. The Chicago White Sox's run to the postseason has been nothing short of remarkable, given they entered the regular season with 500-1 World Series odds, tied for the worst in MLB. Between the long odds and the public's love of an underdog story fueling a betting frenzy, the liability piled up quickly across a variety of futures markets. Chicago enters the ALDS with 18-1 World Series odds, longest on the board.

Odds by DraftKings at time of publication.
